feedback: Approved, and this is the best candidate so far. It is the iteration 7 design (score 929.76, the best raced) resubmitted unchanged: body_length 0.12, mass 0.5, wheel_track 0.12, kp 4.5, ki 0.02, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.1, sensors at y 0.08 with x spread of ±0.05, sensor_size 0.016, line_loss last_direction. Iteration 7 finished 60/60 trials across all three development tracks. Its per-track times were 2.39 s (oval), 2.44 s (s-bend) and 2.63 s (slalom). Its slalom max_error was 0.023, well inside the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 8 raised base_speed to 1.2, and the slalom fell to 18/20 with 2 off-track exits (score 908.2, iteration 8). So 1.1 is the safe speed, and I agree with the Optimizer's choice not to push it further. Another revise round would cost two of the remaining action runs for a gain of a few points at most, and the score is already close to its ceiling. The remaining terms are the single line-loss event per run (about 105 points, untouched by every gain, sensor and speed change so far), rms_error on the s-bend (0.016, about 65 points at full scale), and time. Next iteration, if this races with all tracks finishing and slalom max_error under about 0.025, the only worthwhile test is a small kp change aimed at the s-bend rms. Iteration 4 (kp 5.0, on the heavier body) lowered s-bend rms from 0.0166 to 0.013 but cut slalom progress, so keep the change small. Do not chase line-loss events with gains, because no gain change has moved them.
requested_changes: If this race finishes 60/60 with slalom max_error at or below about 0.025, try kp 4.8 (ki 0.02, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.1 kept). Iteration 4 (kp 5.0 on the heavier body) lowered s-bend rms_error from 0.0166 to 0.013, so a modest kp rise targets the largest tracking term without the slalom loss seen at kp 5.0.

If slalom completion is below 20/20, or slalom max_error passes about 0.03, do not raise kp. Keep kp 4.5 and base_speed 1.1 and resubmit this design, since iteration 8 showed speed 1.2 costs slalom finishes.
